resources.string: Your selected game is %1$s. The advisor currently calculates Texas Hold\'em only; the other variants are being added.
Too many cards are marked for this many opponents.
Your chance (%1$s) is below what the pot requires (%2$s): calling loses money in the long run.
Your chance (%1$s) covers the price of calling (%2$s needed).
Your chance (%1$s) is well ahead of the table (bet from %2$s): build the pot.
Nothing to pay. Your chance (%1$s) is not strong enough to bet (bet from %2$s).
Pot size not entered: compared with an equal share of the pot instead of exact pot odds.
%1$d unseen cards would improve your hand on the next card.
Cards you know are out of this hand (for example shown by a player who folded). They can no longer come on the board.
Optional. Pot = all chips in the middle, including bets this round. To call = what you must add to stay in. Leave \"to call\" empty when nobody has bet.

Learning aid: the advice uses only probability and pot odds and assumes opponents hold random cards. Real players fold weak hands, so when someone bets big their hand is usually stronger than random. Use it only in games where everyone knows.
